comments.author: Iso Tester
comments.body:
INVESTIGATION (read-only; no code changed). Three questions about the plan-review gate, answered by reading the criteria/workflow/engine sources.

Q1 — Does plan review check that plans cite EVIDENCE for new patterns drawn from OSS research?
Finding: Only partially, and in the inverse direction. No criterion requires citing evidence/research when a plan justifies a new pattern by appeal to OSS/industry practice. Closest is T1 (src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_T1.md:10, routing criteria_routing.json:637-671): an AGENTIC overlay that checks (a) prior_art was CONSIDERED before going custom, (b) novelty is justified vs an established approach (anti-repackaging/Rule-of-Three), (c) capability assertions ('library supports X') resolved. T1 pushes you to research prior art before building custom; it does NOT validate an OSS-sourced pattern claim. Surviving T1 findings route to coach Move #2 'prior-art research' (passes.py:527-530). Adjacent: G6 (positive rationale for chosen approach), A1 (anti-cargo-cult). None mandate OSS citations.

Q2 — Does plan review evaluate whether the described implementation matches an ANTIPATTERN?
Finding: Yes, substantially, across several criteria — and it screens BOTH the described implementation approach AND ticket-document quality.
- A1 (plan_review_A1.md:10; routing criteria_routing.json:888-926): the dedicated named-antipattern screen (DSO decider set): golden-hammer, cargo-cult, resume-driven, premature-optimization, NIH, premature-abstraction/Rule-of-Three, YAGNI, config-surface-proliferation. Codebase-grounded (grep evidence required). FP guards: Justified-Complexity needs affirmative evidence; FP7 carve-out = don't flag NIH when rebuilding a designated POC/experiment/reference. Scope: applies_at.levels=['task'], suppress_types=['bug'].
- G6 (plan_review_G6.md): mechanism antipatterns — incomplete logic/data-flow, unhandled edge/empty/concurrent/failure cases, check-then-act-that-is-really-TOCTOU, solving wrong problem, ignoring better alternatives.
- E5 (plan_review_E5.md:10): testing antipatterns — self-authored-oracle/change-detector (always MAJOR), proxy-validation (mock bypasses the new/defaulted path).
- T1: reinvention/anti-repackaging. T8: instruction-locality/pink-elephant (undefined enums/skills/agents). T11: migration antipatterns (blocking DDL, non-batched backfill, non-resumable, dual-write gaps). T12: rollout antipatterns (100%-flip, no rollback).
Note A1's named set is a fixed list (not an open-ended smell catalog); A1 runs on tasks only, not bugs/containers.

comments.author: Iso Tester
comments.body:
Q3 — DESIGN: add an agent doing a NARROW prior-art search to screen for proposed patterns OSS peers have REJECTED (tried-and-abandoned, or never adopted because unnecessary). Expensive (web research). Want: run on architecturally-complex tickets, max once per ticket, ideally re-run on significant architecture revision (v2). Proposed shape: overlay triggered by T1 findings.

Architecture mapping (from reading orchestrator.py, registry.py, sizing.py, attest.py, pass1.py, det_floor.py, runner.py, pai_tools.py, config.py, and gates/plan-review.yaml + executor.py/interpreter.py):

1) TRIGGER (the crux). Inter-criterion finding-dependency DOES NOT EXIST at the criteria layer — route_criteria (orchestrator.py:123-153) selects criteria statically BEFORE any LLM runs; all finders run concurrently in one Pass-1 batch; T1 findings don't exist at selection time; no depends_on/triggered_by field in criteria_routing.json. HOWEVER the WORKFLOW ENGINE supports conditional execution: step 'if:' (executor.py:470-487) and 'branch.when' (interpreter.py:513-539), already used for run_llm and code_grounded branches in gates/plan-review.yaml. So two shapes:
   - Shape A (RECOMMENDED v1): finder-batch overlay like other T-overlays (criteria_routing.json entry + reviewer prompt + batch 'when: include_<ID>'). Inherits verify/decide/coach/checkpoint/signing free. Cannot gate on 'T1 FOUND something' — gate instead on T1's bright-lines + a complexity predicate. Runs whenever (bright-line AND complex) even if T1 clean; bounded by once-per-plan-version cache.
   - Shape B (defer to v2): conditional follow-up step after decide with if:(t1_surfaced && complex). Honors exact intent but bespoke: must expose t1_surfaced + complexity as step outputs and thread findings into coach; no free checkpoint.

2) BIGGEST GAP = web/OSS research tooling. Agentic criteria today get filesystem + rebar ticket tools + configured MCP toolsets only (pai_tools.py:42-207); NO web/GitHub search by default. T1's 'tool-grounded (web/codebase)' is codebase-only in practice. Must add a native web/GitHub-search tool to pai_tools.py (inject via runner extra_tools) OR wire a search MCP via REBAR_LLM_MCP_SERVERS. This is the real net-new work.

3) ONCE-PER-TICKET = mostly free. Checkpoint cache keyed on MATERIAL fingerprint (description+AC+file_impact+children) at .rebar/cache/plan-review/<ticket>/ (sizing.py:240-295); Shape A memoized automatically => once-per-plan-version, auto-invalidates on material edit (also gives crude 're-run on revision' free, but ANY material edit re-triggers, no significant-vs-trivial notion). CAVEAT: cache is LOCAL/git-ignored => once-per-CLONE, not global. For global once-only, persist result into the SIGNED attestation manifest (attest.py build_manifest) or a store event on the tickets branch.

4) COMPLEXITY GATE = reuse existing signals: G5 decomposition triggers (>3 files / >=3 layers / new interface), P4 oversize (>25 AC, >30 file_impact, >24k chars) det_floor.py:309-347, centrality (blast radius) sizing.py:49-57.

5) BUDGET/LATENCY = will bite. Overlay AGENT criteria are SHED FIRST under budget pressure (sizing.py:188-236; cost model prices AGENT at $0.12, web research is far more) => criterion gets dropped before running. Must: bump cost weight, EXEMPT from shed queue, raise REBAR_PLAN_REVIEW_BUDGET; likely a dedicated LLMConfig with higher max_iterations/timeout (defaults 25/600s, config.py:32-40). Latency: runs INLINE in the claim-blocking gate path — a multi-minute web search blocks whoever runs review-plan; consider out-of-band. Per-criterion model override doesn't exist (single base model + runtime size-ladder escalation, runner.py:382-394).

6) REGISTRATION boilerplate: reviewer prompt src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan-review-<ID>.md (execution_mode: agentic) + criteria_routing.json entry + register in CANONICAL_LLM + 'python -m rebar.llm.prompts regenerate-index' (CI drift gate enforces).

RECOMMENDED V1 CUT: Shape A, triggered on T1 bright-lines + complexity gate (not T1 findings); reuse material-fingerprint checkpoint; the only genuinely net-new pieces are the web/OSS-search tool and the budget-shedding exemption/cost-weight. Defer true finding-triggering (Shape B) and significant-vs-trivial revision detection to v2.

SIDE OBSERVATION (not investigated): rebar CLI warns 'unknown key verify.require_plan_review_for_claim ignored (typo?)' on every command against rebar.toml, yet CLAUDE.md says the plan-review claim gate is on for this project. Worth verifying the config key name is correct — the gate may be silently inactive.

No ticket created yet; offered to write this up as an epic/story with AC + v1/v2 split or prototype the web-research tool wiring first.

comments.author: Iso Tester
comments.body:
Brainstorm + decomposition + derisk spike for alto-fruit-punch (d251) — Provision AWS Gerrit + rebar MCP; lock GitHub main to Gerrit (the code-review dogfood prerequisite).

ARC
- Re-grounded in the prior decision record (session_log slap-tripe-vat / 9dba): Gerrit-on-AWS as the un-bypassable LLM-Review merge gate, GitHub as a read-only mirror (Go topology). Independent research (GitHub-native vs GerritHub vs self-host; Gerrit project health) was run; it pressure-tested but did NOT overturn the locked decision — the rationale (kernel-vote<->label mapping, copyCondition cost lever, submitWholeTopic, exactly-one-writer topology, prior art) holds. Premise challenge dropped.
- Locked the open design questions: live PoC (priorities: function+integrity > cost > reliability/reuse-if-free); freeze-and-restore, no break-glass; AWS justified (existing acct); repo public; org free -> repo-level lockdown with trusted-admin-override accepted; domain rebar.solutions.navateam.com; infra under infra/ excluded from distribution.
- Ran a prior-art research spike (4 agents): converged reference architecture = docker-compose Gerrit (official image) + nginx (NOT Caddy, %2F) + external MCP voter on Set Review REST + core Apache replication plugin (non-force) + repo-level ruleset lockdown + cost-lean single Graviton box (no ALB/NAT, gp3, SSM Parameter Store, roll-your-own Terraform).

DECOMPOSITION (created): epic d251 now has 7 child stories S1-S7 with ACs/deps. S1 TF base; S2 Gerrit+MCP deploy+nginx/TLS; S3 project+LLM-Review label+submit-req+submitWholeTopic; S4 bot identity+events+voter (proven pipe); S5 Gerrit->GitHub replication; S6 GitHub repo lockdown; S7 e2e proof+backup/restore+monitoring+runbooks. Sequence S1<-S2<-S3<-{S4,S5}; S5<-S6; {S4,S5,S6}<-S7.

DERISK EXPERIMENTS (real AWS CLI as root of 896586841071/us-east-1 + local Docker + gh) — all green:
- E1: default VPC vpc-01fb22d3dd50a364c; AL2023 arm64 AMI via SSM param; t4g.large in all AZs; run-instances --dry-run of the exact shape OK.
- E2: PUBLIC Route53 zone solutions.navateam.com exists in-account (Z05558453EZPQLHKC20IQ) -> the subdomain is a simple A record.
- E3: SSM SecureString put/get(decrypt)/delete validated.
- E4: Gerrit 3.14.1 boots on arm64 (pin a PATCH tag — bare 3.14/3.13 don't exist); submit-req predicate label:LLM-Review=MAX AND -has:unresolved parses (HTTP 200) on live Gerrit; nginx %2F-safe proxy passes nginx -t.
- E5: navapbc/rebar public, Issues off, 0 deploy keys, I'm admin; org FREE (repo-level only); EXISTING ruleset main-protection (PR+status-checks) must be REPLACED (incompatible with mirror lock); DeployKey-bypass ruleset payload shape confirmed.

Tickets updated with findings: S1/S5 derisk comments; S2 pinned to a real arm64 patch tag + nginx note; S3 empirically-validated config; S6 add 'replace main-protection' AC + free-org/admin-override note; epic decisions+derisk summary comment.

NEXT: run plan-review on the epic + each child to earn claim attestations, then S1 is the ready entry point. Cleanup: removed the local gerrit-derisk test container; Colima left running (I started it for E4 — co-tenant containers keycloak/parity-scan are present; `colima stop` if you want it down).
